subject.title: Telegram: Auto-reply to unauthorized group senders with admin contact instructions

question: Should OpenClaw add an opt-in Telegram reply for non-allowlisted group senders, and what cooldown, admin-contact, raw-ID, topic, and default-silent semantics should it use?
rationale: The request changes behavior at an authorization-denial boundary and can expose identifiers or amplify messages, so automation cannot safely choose the permanent product/security contract.

options.title: Add Opt-In Rate-Limited Notice
options.body: Add a Telegram plugin setting for denied-sender onboarding replies with per-chat/topic/sender cooldown, configurable admin-contact wording, and explicit raw-ID handling.

options.title: Route Through Operator Audit
options.body: Keep unauthorized senders silent and satisfy visibility through owner notification or denied-inbound audit work such as https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/77546.

options.title: Keep Silent Denial
options.body: Decline sender-facing replies for now and document groupAllowFrom, logs, and manual ID discovery as the supported secure posture.

recommendation.title: Add Opt-In Rate-Limited Notice
recommendation.body: Add a Telegram plugin setting for denied-sender onboarding replies with per-chat/topic/sender cooldown, configurable admin-contact wording, and explicit raw-ID handling.

likelyOwner.reason: Vincent Koc owns the current blamed denial helper, skip branch, tests, docs, and schema snapshot that this product/security decision would change.
